a1.claim_boundary: A1 is a retained failed hosted automation run. It completed neither CodeQL analysis nor the requested independent code/security review and is never rewritten as a pass.

claims.qualification: The population covers 192 mutations and 22 restart/kill cases, including 14 precise internal failpoints, for the exact A3 identity; it is not a proof against unenumerated faults.
claims.statement: The fresh A3 population attempted all 214 enumerated adversarial cases exactly once and both the driver and independent validator report 214 passed and 0 failed.

claims.qualification: A1 is 150/64 under its frozen validator and 146/68 under the stricter diagnostic; A2 is 214/0 by the driver and 210/4 independently. Supersession does not erase either failure.
claims.statement: A1 and A2 remain published as failed and superseded and no A1 or A2 attempt or outcome was reused by A3.

claims.qualification: A2 completed all 17 required tool outcomes, then its final gate failed without retry on one unwaived CodeQL rust/cleartext-logging result. Failures, unavailable tools, warnings, and retries remain visible. Automation does not prove security, correctness, exhaustive coverage, or absence of vulnerabilities and is not an independent human review.
claims.statement: The checksum-closed automated quality history records bounded local and hosted tests, audits, static checks, and fuzz campaigns; hosted security A1 and A2 are both retained as failed runs.

claims.qualification: The signature authenticates validation-candidate bytes and project continuity only. The archive is locally deterministic and the verifier reproduced byte-identically in two same-host builds; cross-host and arbitrary-path executor byte identity remain unestablished.
claims.statement: The final validation candidate is bound by its exact signed manifest, detached signature, archive and sidecar, verification/signing/extraction records, source inventories, SBOM, provenance, and build-reproduction inventory.

claims.qualification: The failed v2 population remains 52/48 and is not rewritten. V3 is a single-host descriptive result: 1/2/4 are physical-core points, 8/16 are oversubscribed, and the profile is observational rather than causal. No universal speedup or hardware-supercomputer claim follows.
claims.statement: The complete v3 fixed-work scaling population contains exactly 100 attempted, retained, and successful outcomes over lanes 1, 2, 4, 8, and 16; its bound profile identifies finalization as the largest retained median executor phase.

claims.qualification: Runner, job, and hashed host-fingerprint distinction is not physical-host attestation, three independent administrative domains, or source-to-binary reproducibility.
claims.statement: Three distinct GitHub-hosted VM jobs reproduced the exact signed release/workload and the final aggregate is claim-eligible.

claims.qualification: The review shares the same AI system, repository, host environment, and project authority; it is not human, organizational, administrative-domain, provider, or environment independence. Human review remains not_performed/open. Until a new signed revision fixes the finding, omit --report and capture stdout to a trusted new path that cannot overlap the result, verified inputs, or input store.
claims.statement: A candidate-bound, procedurally separate AI-assisted code/security review was completed with one retained low-severity verifier report-path finding, one informational observation, and no critical, high, or medium findings.

claims.qualification: This is one small external integration and correctness case, not workload generality, classification quality, production fitness, or a performance claim.
claims.statement: One final-candidate UCI Iris workload capture was accepted by the executor, standalone verifier, and an independent exact oracle.

claims.qualification: Commercial evaluation means a technical package and optional services; it does not imply proprietary software, a customer, payment, SLA, counsel approval, or a paid design partner.
claims.statement: A release-ready Apache-2.0 technical evaluation package preserves the open-verifier and open-executor boundary and exposes consent-based design-partner intake.

claims.qualification: The artifact is a technical paper and is not represented as peer reviewed.
claims.statement: The final technical paper centers on the replay-gated execution contract and binds the final evidence identities.

claims.qualification: At signing time the newly staged evidence, validation record, and signature are not claimed as live or independently HTTP-retrieved. A separate checksum-closed post-deployment retrieval attestation and site audit are required. URL availability never authenticates bytes by itself; readers must verify pinned digests and signatures.
claims.statement: The publication-ready release index binds locally verified staged input bytes to planned HTTPS locations and records the planned validation-record and detached-signature URLs.

external_workload.claim_boundary: This is one small external integration and exact-correctness workload, not workload generality, biological classification quality, production fitness, or a performance claim.

hosted_reproduction.claim_boundary: Three ephemeral GitHub-hosted Ubuntu 24.04 VM jobs from one runner image family reproduced the exact signed release workload. Job, runner, and hashed fingerprint distinction is not physical-host attestation, three administrative domains, or source-to-binary reproducibility.

independent_code_security_review.independence_basis: A separately assigned review agent follows a read-only, candidate-bound review procedure and reports findings independently of the implementation task, while sharing the same AI system, repository, host environment, and project authority.

known_low_finding.current_mitigation: Omit --report and capture stdout to a trusted new, non-symlink, non-overlapping path distinct from --result, every verified input, and the input store.
known_low_finding.required_fix: Publish --report with executor-style create-new/no-replace semantics, reject symlinks, existing targets, and overlap with --result, verified inputs, or the input store, add interruption and overlap regression tests, and ship only in a new signed candidate revision.

limitations: This is procedural separation, not human, organizational, administrative-domain, provider, or environment independence.
The review uses the same execution environment, repository, AI system, and project authority as the implementation work.
AI-assisted review can miss defects and does not prove security or absence of vulnerabilities.
Hosted security automation is corroborating evidence, not a human review.

independent_human_review.claim_boundary: No independent human code/security review has been performed. The opportunity remains open and visible, but it is not a publication blocker for the bounded procedurally separate AI-assisted review claim.

performance_profile.claim_boundary: The profile ranks instrumented phases by retained wall-clock medians. It is observational and does not establish CPU, storage, or system-level causality.

candidate_signing_record.claim_boundary: The candidate signature authenticates the exact validation-candidate manifest bytes and project continuity only; it does not certify correctness, security, performance, independent review, hardware, or fitness.
candidate_signing_record.verification_scope: The retained record includes an operator-observed pre-sign full pass, a post-sign independent static replay of pre-sign gate behavior, a retained post-sign full pass, correct-namespace verification, and a wrong-namespace negative control. The static replay does not establish temporal ordering before signing.

release_identity.reproducibility_boundary: The archive is deterministically reproducible in the recorded local environment and the standalone verifier reproduced byte-identically in two same-host builds. Cross-host executor byte identity and arbitrary-path executor byte identity are not established.

scaling.claim_boundary: The 100/100 v3 result is a single-host descriptive fixed-work population. Only lanes 1, 2, and 4 are physical-core points; lanes 8 and 16 are oversubscribed on four cores. It is not a universal speedup or hardware-supercomputer claim.

prior_failed_v2.qualification: The frozen v2 verdict remains 52 success and 48 failure. A later diagnostic found the 48 failures were caused by an over-strict transient current-CPU observer, but the diagnostic never replaces the frozen v2 verdict.
